query: For high-entropy alloys used in thermal-insulation applications, what testable hypothesis could be made about an unspecified predictive approach for accurately identifying materials with low phonon thermal conductivity? The hypothesis should explain why the approach would work, predict its improvement over current predictions, define its applicability limits, identify supporting evidence, and specify a decisive experimental benchmark and outcome that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: A predictive approach that quantitatively incorporates descriptors of configurational disorder—such as local lattice distortion, atomic mass variance, and anharmonicity of vibrational modes—will more accurately identify high-entropy alloys with intrinsically low phonon thermal conductivity compared to conventional models that rely on averaged properties.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic or near‐equiatomic high-entropy alloys exhibiting high configurational disorder in a single-phase or nearly single-phase state without significant phase segregation.
generation.intervention: Apply the advanced predictive method to a broad candidate set of HEAs and select top candidates predicted to have severely enhanced phonon scattering (i.e., lower thermal conductivity). Synthesize these candidate alloys for thermal conductivity measurements.
generation.conditions: Measurements conducted at room temperature and elevated temperatures representative of thermal-insulation applications; alloys must be in a thermodynamically stable, single-phase state; conventional phonon transport regimes apply and electronic conduction is not dominant.
generation.structural_mediator: Local lattice distortions and mass disorder induce enhanced phonon scattering, thereby reducing the phonon mean free path.
generation.mechanism: By explicitly incorporating indicators of atomic-scale disorder (e.g., atomic mass variance, local distortion parameters from lattice dynamics calculations) and anharmonic phonon interactions, the predictive method captures scattering mechanisms more effectively than conventional average-property based models. This leads to more accurate forecasts of very low phonon thermal conductivity in the selected HEAs.
generation.predicted_outcome: HEAs identified via the predictive approach will demonstrate a measured phonon thermal conductivity that is at least ~20% lower than that predicted by conventional approaches and lower than that of HEAs selected without using these refined descriptors.
generation.baseline: Conventional prediction methodologies that average material properties and do not specifically account for local disorder-driven anharmonic phonon scattering.
generation.boundary: This approach is anticipated to be applicable primarily to high-entropy alloys with significant configurational disorder and single-phase structures; it may be less effective or inapplicable in systems with marked phase separation or where electronic heat conduction dominates.
generation.uncertainty: While the improvement margin is predicted to be around 20%, the exact quantitative gain and the precise compositional boundaries remain uncertain until validated by experiments.

falsification_experiment.design: Use the predictive approach to screen and select a set of candidate HEAs predicted to exhibit ultra-low phonon thermal conductivity. Synthesize these candidates ensuring phase purity and stable microstructure. Measure the thermal conductivity (specifically the phonon contribution) using laser flash analysis and complementary techniques (e.g., time-domain thermoreflectance). Compare these measurements against both conventional predictions and the advanced model’s forecasts.
measurements: Thermal diffusivity and conductivity via laser flash analysis
Assessment of lattice disorder (e.g., via EXAFS or PDF analysis)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the measured phonon thermal conductivity of the synthesized HEAs does not show at least a 20% reduction (improvement) relative to conventional model predictions, or if candidate materials perform similarly to those chosen by standard approaches, then the hypothesis that the advanced predictive approach offers superior identification of low-thermal-conductivity HEAs is falsified.
